title: Zero-Double-Free Invariants and O(1) Allocation in a C++ Sub-Allocator
topic: It s all about the allocator
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We present a lightweight sub-allocator that guarantees a zero-double-free invariant while achieving constant-time allocation and deallocation for single-object requests. The allocator maintains a singly-linked free list over a statically sized buffer, ensuring that each node is returned to the pool exactly once. We formally prove that the free list never contains duplicate entries and that the contiguous arena invariant holds after every operation. Theoretical analysis shows that allocation and deallocation run in $O(1)$ time, while the overall memory footprint is bounded by the compile-time capacity. No dynamic memory is requested from the system; the allocator is fully deterministic and suitable for real-time or embedded contexts. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/cpp-systems-core/tree/main/algorithms/20261119_200111_it_s_all_about_the_allocator}
